collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager asks three people whether to move their hut near the stream and gets three answers: ask a fourth, or decide alone.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) can't decide whether to move (subject.his/her) hut closer to the stream. (subject.He/she) asks (friend), who says, "Yes! Fresh water every morning!" Then (subject.he/she) asks (third), who says, "Absolutely not. Mosquitoes." Then (subject.he/she) asks (villager), a third villager, who says, "What hut?" (subject) now knows less than when (subject.he/she) started.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) asks (villager2), a fourth person, who says, "Do whatever makes you happy." (subject) groans. "That's the least useful one yet!" On the walk home, though, (subject.he/she) notices (subject.he/she) was disappointed every time someone said "don't move." So (subject.he/she) moves. There are a lot of mosquitoes. There's also fresh water every morning. (subject.He/she) is happy, and itchy.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) sits by (subject.his/her) hut until sunset, thinking. In the end (subject.he/she) stays put. Not because anyone told (subject.him/her) to. (subject.He/she) just likes the view of the sea from here too much. Nobody asks (subject.him/her) about it again, which is a relief, because (subject.he/she) couldn't explain it if they did.
